A 38-year-old female presents to the emergency department with progressive leg weakness that has
led to an inability to stand. She is a school teacher in Alaska and frequently goes hiking and camping.
Recently, she returned from a camping trip where she drank from mountain streams and hiked through
tall brush. Two days ago, she was involved in a motor vehicle accident but did not seek medical care.
She reports a recent episode of diarrhea but is otherwise healthy. Her temperature is 98.7°F (37.5°C),
blood pressure is 117/79 mmHg, pulse is 103/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is
98% on room air. On physical exam, she is anxious, with 1/5 strength in her lower extremities and 2/5
strength in her trunk muscles. She also reports symmetrical tingling and prickling sensations in her
lower extremities. Laboratory studies are as follows: Hemoglobin: 15 g/dL Hematocrit: 43% Leukocyte
count: 6,500/mm³ with normal differential Platelet count: 194,000/mm³ Serum: Na■: 138 mEq/L Cl■:
102 mEq/L K■: 4.4 mEq/L HCO■■: 24 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 120 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.0
mg/dL Ca²■: 10.2 mg/dL pH: 7.44 PaCO■: 10 mmHg PaO■: 90 mmHg AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L The
patient reports difficulty breathing. An arterial blood gas reveals: pH: 7.35 PaCO■: 30 mmHg PaO■: 80
mmHg She is intubated and admitted to the ICU. Which of the following is most closely associated with
the likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Exposure to tick-borne neurotoxins during camping (B)
Contaminated mountain stream water ingestion (C) Consuming meats cooked over a campfire (D)
Post-viral autoimmune demyelination (E) Spinal cord injury from the recent motor vehicle accident (F)
